title: (A)I Am Not a Lawyer, But. . .: Engaging Legal Experts towards Responsible LLM Policies for Legal Advice

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative analysis of legal expert workshop deliberations based on realistic legal queries, identifying concerns around structural stereotypes, discrimination, and the skewed representation of majority demographics over minority views.

Eliciting expert feedback during case-based reasoning workshops, highlighting how LLM advice may disproportionately reflect the values of specific cultures and fail to recognize that what is morally neutral in one culture may be problematic in another.
Qualitative coding of expert discussions revealing concerns that LLMs trained predominantly on English data inherently favor the values, perspectives, and contexts of English-speaking populations.

Analyzing expert evaluations of LLM responses to identify assumptions about users' income, time, and access to resources (e.g., incorrectly recommending actions that assume the user can afford private legal representation or extensive travel).
